observation.visible_scene: A residential backyard lawn: a weathered wooden fence runs along the left, a brown wooden shed/coop with dark wire mesh occupies the right, and a house with a green bucket and potted plants sits in the background. Three pigeons stand on the grass. One large foreground pigeon (light grey body, black wing bars, iridescent green-purple neck) stands right of center facing right. Two smaller pigeons are in the mid-ground behind it, one on the left and one on the right.
visible_changes: The foreground pigeon stays in essentially the same spot from first to last frame, facing right, with only minor head turns and small posture adjustments; no walking or takeoff is seen.
The left mid-ground pigeon shifts slightly rightward and changes its head/tail posture over the clip (tail raised at times, head moving from lowered to upright).

The right mid-ground pigeon alternates between lowering its head toward the grass and raising it upright; by the later frames it has moved right and now stands close beside the left mid-ground pigeon with its head up.

Background landmarks (fence, green bucket, house windows, shed edge) remain in consistent positions across the excerpt, so the camera is effectively static with at most negligible handheld drift; the apparent changes are bird motion, not scene motion.
No editing cut is visible; the segment reads as continuous footage.
outside_clip_unknowns: What, if anything, the pigeons are pecking or eating on the grass.
Whether the head-lowering motions are feeding or just alertness.
Any motion or events before the first frame or after the last frame (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the right mid-ground pigeon's head-up vs head-down changes (pecking, looking, or balancing) is not determinable from the frames alone.
Minor apparent scale/position differences of the foreground pigeon could be tiny posture changes or slight camera jitter; not confidently separable.
Relative spacing of the two mid-ground pigeons changes gradually, but precise walking steps are not resolvable at this frame rate.
